questions.text: What is the fundamental focus of PPS?
questions.correct: Result and completed achievement
questions.hint: "The present perfect simple is fundamentally about results." ✅

questions.text: What does "I have been studying" emphasise compared to "I have studied"?
opts: The process and duration — still in progress
questions.correct: The process and duration — still in progress
questions.hint: PPC = emphasises the ongoing process and its duration. ✅

questions.text: "I have lived in Uralsk for two years" — why PPS for "live"?
questions.correct: "Live" is stative — can't take continuous
questions.hint: "'Live' is a stative verb that cannot take the continuous." ✅ (though "been living" is also natural)

questions.text: Kamila says "I've written 200 words" vs "I've been writing for 2 hours" — the difference?
opts: "Written 200 words" = result/count; "been writing for 2 hours" = process/effort
questions.correct: "Written 200 words" = result/count; "been writing for 2 hours" = process/effort
questions.hint: PPS = result/count (200 words). PPC = process/effort (2 hours of work). ✅

questions.text: What does "I have been studying English since September" tell us about the studying?
opts: It started in September and is still ongoing
questions.correct: It started in September and is still ongoing
questions.hint: PPC + SINCE = started at starting point, still ongoing now. ✅

questions.text: Aliya says "We've been conducting a three-year study." — PPC because:
opts: The study is ongoing — still in progress after three years
questions.correct: The study is ongoing — still in progress after three years
questions.hint: "We've been conducting a three-year study." — PPC, still ongoing. ✅

questions.text: How many students has Kamila interviewed for her thesis?
questions.correct: Twelve
questions.hint: "I've interviewed twelve students so far." ✅

questions.text: What has Aliya's team established that didn't exist before?
opts: A monitoring network across five regions
questions.correct: A monitoring network across five regions
questions.hint: "We've established a monitoring network across five regions of Kazakhstan that hasn't existed before." ✅

questions.text: What has the government passed in the last three years?
opts: Two new pieces of environmental legislation
questions.correct: Two new pieces of environmental legislation
questions.hint: "The government has passed two new pieces of environmental legislation in the last three years." ✅

questions.text: Why has the full pollution study not been completed?
opts: The team has been refining the methodology as they go
questions.correct: The team has been refining the methodology as they go
questions.hint: "The full study hasn't been completed — we've been refining the methodology as we go." ✅

questions.text: Kamila says she has finally started to enjoy what?
opts: The whole process of academic research
questions.correct: The whole process of academic research
questions.hint: "I've finally started to enjoy the process — which I haven't always done." ✅

questions.text: Daniyar says he has been doing what since starting at WKU?
questions.correct: Code-switching (alternating languages)
questions.hint: "I've been doing it since I started at WKU." — referring to code-switching that Kamila mentioned. ✅

questions.text: "She has finished the report." — PPS because:
opts: The result matters now — report is done
questions.correct: The result matters now — report is done
questions.hint: PPS = completed action with present relevance. The report exists and is done. ✅

questions.text: "I have seen him yesterday." — Error:
opts: "Yesterday" = specific past time → need Past Simple: "I saw him"
questions.correct: "Yesterday" = specific past time → need Past Simple: "I saw him"
questions.hint: Specific past time → Past Simple. ✅ "I SAW him yesterday." ✅

questions.text: "She ___ (know) him FOR ten years." — correct form:
questions.correct: has known
questions.hint: "know" = stative → PPS. "She HAS KNOWN him for ten years." ✅ (NOT "has been knowing")

questions.text: "She's been writing 3 papers." — Error:
opts: "3 papers" = counting → must use PPS: "She's written 3 papers"
questions.correct: "3 papers" = counting → must use PPS: "She's written 3 papers"
questions.hint: ✅ Counting = PPS. "She's WRITTEN 3 papers." ✅

questions.text: FOR vs SINCE: "She's been here ___ three weeks." Choose.
questions.correct: for
questions.hint: "three weeks" = duration → FOR. "She's been here FOR three weeks." ✅

questions.text: "You look pale. Have you been feeling OK?" — PPC because:
opts: PPC explains visible state (pale appearance) through ongoing condition
questions.correct: PPC explains visible state (pale appearance) through ongoing condition
questions.hint: PPC = explains present visible state. "Have you been feeling OK?" (explains pallor) ✅

questions.text: "I've lived here for 3 years" vs "I've been living here for 3 years" — which is correct?
questions.correct: Both are correct — different emphasis
questions.hint: "Lived" (PPS) = settled state/credential. "Been living" (PPC) = ongoing process. Both natural. ✅

questions.text: "How long have you been waiting?" — Why PPC?
opts: The question asks about the duration of an ongoing activity
questions.correct: The question asks about the duration of an ongoing activity
questions.hint: "How long" asks about duration of ongoing activity → PPC. "How long have you BEEN WAITING?" ✅

questions.text: "Immersed in the activity." "Immersed" means:
questions.correct: Deeply absorbed in
questions.hint: "immersed" = deeply involved; surrounded by and fully engaged with something.

questions.text: "She's been developing her skills." "Developing" (PPC) emphasises:
opts: The process of development is ongoing
questions.correct: The process of development is ongoing
questions.hint: PPC = process focus. "Has been developing" = still in the process of developing. ✅

questions.text: "The choice comes down to intent." "Intent" means:
opts: What you aim to communicate; your purpose
questions.correct: What you aim to communicate; your purpose
questions.hint: "intent" = what you intend; your purpose or aim in making a choice.

questions.text: "Presenting a credential." "Credential" means:
opts: A qualification proving competence or experience
questions.correct: A qualification proving competence or experience
questions.hint: "credential" = evidence of qualification, expertise, or achievement.

questions.text: "The convention in British English." "Convention" means:
opts: An accepted standard way of doing something in a context
questions.correct: An accepted standard way of doing something in a context
questions.hint: "convention" = an accepted or standard practice within a particular context or field.
